rows.question: We discovered an ordinary CPF overpayment last week, but cannot yet locate the payment record. May we use the discovery date to set our refund deadline, and can we wait for CPF Board to refund us before returning the employee's share?
rows.before:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### CPF Board — CPF contributions

**Status:** Evidence verified

**CPF employer refund timing and application requirements** (party in scope: Employer)
- **CPF rule explanation:** Refund requests for CPF contributions generally must be made immediately and no later than one year from payment; the “PAYMENTS RECEIVED ON” field identifies the payment date. For conditional wages, the one-year period instead runs from when the wages are due to be repaid to the employer, as stated in employment terms or a mutual agreement, and that date must be entered in the application. Before applying, the employer must return the employee share directly to the employee. CPF Board effects refunds only to the extent of funds available in the employee’s CPF account. Excess Additional Wage ceiling contributions should be claimed promptly; excess CPF Annual Limit contributions paid from 2023 are automatically refunded to the employer’s Direct Debit Account from February 2024. The general and entire-submission application deadline is one year from contribution payment, using the “PAYMENTS RECEIVED ON” record field. Conditional-wage refunds use the repayment due date, not the contribution payment date. The employer must first return the employee share where applicable; refunds depend on funds available in employee CPF accounts. Excess Additional Wage ceiling contributions are a prompt-application category. CPF Annual Limit excess contributions paid from 2023 are refunded automatically to the employer from February 2024; this is distinct from an application for an AW-ceiling refund. For case-specific application, consider: Refund category and CPF payment date. For conditional wages, the contractual or mutually agreed repayment due date. Whether the employee share was returned and funds remain available in CPF account(s). For AW or annual-limit excess, the relevant year and excess category. Do not infer a refund deadline when the payment date, conditional-wage repayment date or calendar anniversary is unclear. The source does not establish that a particular refund application will be accepted or the amount CPF Board will refund. [CPFB | Applying for refund of CPF contributions](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/compliance-and-rectifications/applying-for-refund-of-cpf-contributions)

**Source:** CPFB | Applying for refund of CPF contributions (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF employer refund timing and application requirements): Any request for refund of CPF contributions paid must be made immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment of the CPF contributions. You can refer to the “PAYMENTS RECEIVED ON” field in your record of payment to determine the date of payment.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF employer refund timing and application requirements): Any request for refund of CPF contributions paid on conditional wages must be made immediately and no later than one year from the date wages are supposed to be repaid to the employer. This will be the date stated in the terms of employment or based on mutual agreement
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF employer refund timing and application requirements): You’re responsible to refund the employee’s share of CPF contributions (where applicable) directly to your employee before submitting the application.

rows.question: An employee covered by the Employment Act has completed four months of service, supplied the required medical certificate and informed us within twenty-four hours. Is the statutory entitlement already fourteen outpatient sick-leave days plus sixty hospitalisation days?
rows.before:
### Statutory Directive: Annual Leave and Paid Sick / Hospitalisation Leave Statutory Entitlements

**Governing Authority**: **MOM** | **Legislation**: **Employment Act 1968 (Section 88A & Section 89)**

---

#### 1. Statutory Principle
Employees covered by the Employment Act 1968 are eligible for paid annual leave after at least 3 months of service, including probation; annual leave is pro-rated by completed months where applicable, with 7 days for the first 12 months and one additional day for each subsequent 12 months up to 14 days. Paid sick leave is available after at least 3 months and is pro-rated by service until the full outpatient and hospitalisation entitlement applies at 6 months.

---

#### 2. Key Rules, Thresholds & Compliance Mandates
* Paid Annual Leave (Section 88A): Eligibility begins after 3 months of service, including probation. For 3 to 12 months of service, pro-rate by completed months using 7 days for the first service year; exclude approved unpaid-leave periods from the pro-rating calculation. Entitlement increases by 1 day for each subsequent 12 months of service, up to 14 days.
* Paid Outpatient Sick Leave (Section 89): Up to 14 days per calendar year if certified by an approved medical practitioner. The graduated outpatient/hospitalisation entitlements are 5/15 days at 3 months, 8/30 at 4 months, 11/45 at 5 months, and 14/60 at 6 months or more.
* Paid Hospitalisation Leave (Section 89): The 60-day maximum includes outpatient sick leave; the two limits are not additive. Actual available leave is capped by the applicable entitlement after leave already taken and qualifying certification.
* Public Holidays (Section 88): 11 statutory gazetted public holidays per year. If required to work on a public holiday, an employee is entitled to an extra day of basic salary or a day off in lieu.

---

#### 3. Official Statutory Source & Verification
* Verified against Employment Act 1968 Section 88A & Section 89 using the registered official source record.
* Review the **Statutory Citations & "Why"** tab for full legal references and citations.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Evidence verified

**MAS LFMC CEO and Director appointment and subsequent notification requirements** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** The current MAS LFMC Compliance Toolkit row 3 says an LFMC must seek prior MAS approval using Form 11 before appointing a Chief Executive Officer or Director, or before changing a Director’s appointment nature from Non-Executive to Executive; already being on the board does not remove approval for that change. Row 17 is a separate subsequent notification: it covers CEO or Director resignation, an Executive-to-Non-Executive change, changed CEO/Director particulars, and changed business interests or shareholdings provided in Form 11. Row 17 gives “As soon as practicable” for these notifications; its additional no-later-than-14-days limit is specifically attached to the resignation in item (i). The toolkit applies to Licensed Fund Management Companies and identifies the SFA and LCBR requirements in its scope. Row 3 calls for prior approval; row 17 separately concerns subsequent notifications and must not be substituted for row 3. Its 14-day time limit applies to item (i), resignation. This toolkit is not exhaustive and excludes requirements outside the SFA and fund-level requirements. The toolkit revision date is not a legal commencement date; this summary does not establish historic requirements. For case-specific application, consider: Whether the firm is an LFMC. Whether the person is a CEO or Director and whether the action is an initial appointment, Director nature change, resignation or later particulars change. General current toolkit guidance only; verify the applicable SFA provisions, licence conditions and current MAS requirements for a specific LFMC. Do not apply this row to VCFMs or other CMS licence holders without a source covering that regime. [LICENSED FUND MANAGEMENT COMPANIES](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit-lfmcs29-may-2026-clean.pdf)

rows.question: Our venture capital fund manager has not confirmed its financial year-end. Can we use the calendar-year nil-misconduct return deadline for Form 25A and assume that filing Form 25A also completes every reporting obligation of the funds we manage?

### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence is incomplete for one or more material issues.

**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Evidence verified

**Venture Capital Fund Manager** (party in scope: Not established)

**MAS VCFM annual declaration and Form 25A reporting requirements** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** MAS’s current VCFM compliance toolkit says a venture capital fund manager must submit Form 25A, an annual declaration of changes to key appointments, assets under management, investor types and numbers, fund types, and deals, within one month after its financial year end. The toolkit cites Regulation 14(6) of the Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations. The due date for a specific manager depends on its financial year end. [VENTURE CAPITAL FUND MANAGERS](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit--vcfms29-may-2026-clean.pdf)

**MAS VCFM nil misconduct return requirements** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** MAS FAQ 13 says that financial institutions covered by SFA 04-N11 are not required to submit a nil misconduct declaration for the calendar year ending 31 December 2026, notwithstanding the existing Notice wording. The Misconduct Reporting Notices effective 1 January 2027 also do not require nil declarations. If you mean a different reporting year, identify that calendar year: this FAQ passage does not establish its deadline. [FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (“FAQs”) ON](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas/regulations-and-financial-stability/regulations-guidance-and-licensing/financial-advisers/faq/faqs-on-misconduct-reporting-notices-under-the-faa-ia-and-sfa.pdf)

**MAS VCFM toolkit scope and fund-level requirements** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** MAS describes the VCFM toolkit as a reference for common applications, forms and submissions under the Securities and Futures Act. MAS says it is not exhaustive and expressly excludes reporting obligations outside the SFA and fund-level requirements. Therefore, Form 25A does not establish that every reporting obligation of each managed fund is complete. Identify applicable fund-level requirements separately for each fund and relevant activity; this source does not provide a complete fund-level checklist. [VENTURE CAPITAL FUND MANAGERS](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit--vcfms29-may-2026-clean.pdf)

**Source:** Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title) (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Venture Capital Fund Manager): If your company wishes to conduct fund management activities regulated under the Securities and Futures Act 2001 (SFA) , it must apply to be a licensed fund management company (LFMC) that holds a capital markets services (CMS) licence.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Venture Capital Fund Manager): If your company solely manages venture capital funds, it may apply to be an LFMC that operates under the simplified venture capital fund manager (VCFM) regime.

- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports MAS VCFM nil misconduct return requirements): 13 Are FIs required to submit to MAS a declaration of nil return of misconduct of
representatives or broking staff for the calendar year ended 31 December 2026?
No. MAS does not require FIs to submit a declaration of nil return of misconduct of
representatives or broking staff for the calendar year ending 31 December 2026,
notwithstanding the requirement under paragraph 6 of the following Notices:
• FAA-N14 Notice on Reporting of Misconduct of Representatives by Financial Advisers
• MAS 504 Notice on Reporting of Misconduct of Broking Staff by Insurance Brokers
• SFA 04-N11 Notice on Reporting of Misconduct of Representatives by Holders of
Capital Markets Services Licence and Exempt Financial Institutions
Under the Misconduct Reporting Notices, which take effect on 1 January 2027, FIs are not
required to submit to MAS a declaration of nil return of misconduct of representatives or
broking staff.
